newsitem.title: USA: U.S Sept CPI gains affirm benign inflation picture.
newsitem.headline: U.S Sept CPI gains affirm benign inflation picture.

text.p: U.S. consumer prices advanced at a firm but tolerable pace in September, indicating inflation remained subdued heading into the fourth quarter of 1996, economists said on Wednesday.
"These numbers are really fairly benign," said Anthony Chan, chief economist at Banc One Investment Advisors Inc. "The factors that kicked in are not factors one would expect to continue."
The U.S. Labor Department said consumer prices rose at a 0.3 percent pace in both overall and core rates in September.

The gains were exactly in line with expectations and caused barely a ripple in the markets, but economists expressed relief at the tepid nature of a widely anticipated bounceback from meager August price gains.

Apparel prices, which fell by a hefty 1.4 percent in August rose by only 0.5 percent in the September report despite suggestions by the Bureau of Labor Statistics that a greater rebound may be forthcoming.
Airline fares rose by 2.9 percent in September, the largest gain since February, but economists said the rise was likely to be temporary.
"Airline fares were obviously a strong contributor but everyone knows that's not going to be sustainable moving forward," said Chan.
"The 10 percent excise tax is a one-shot thing," he added, referring to an additional airline cost which had been expected to boost September airfares.
Overall and core consumer prices posted paltry 0.1 percent gains in August and analysts said before Wednesday's report that they would look at the August and September releases in tandem.
When taken together, the subdued nature of the August and September reports suggested to some that forthcoming October prices could post strong gains.
They said a steady rise in energy prices has yet to fully show through at the consumer level.

"It's going to be spread over two months," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc, referring to the rebound from August levels. "It sets the stage for a slight deterioration in the inflation outlook, but it's still very slight."
Other analysts said any deterioration will ultimately depend on the U.S. consumer who remained largely dormant throughout the third quarter despite steady wage and job gains.

"Going forward, what we are saying is that there has been a marked slowdown in domestic demand and that should cap any possible increase in inflationary pressures as we go forward," said Kathy Bostjancic, money market analyst at UBS Securities Inc.
